html:
Nukuleka, a village on the lagoon of Tongatapu, is held by many archaeologists to be the first human settlement in Polynesia. People of the Lapita culture lived there from about 2,800 years ago.

They came by canoe from the west, through Fiji, bringing decorated pottery, pigs, chickens and crops. Within a few generations they spread to the rest of Tonga and to Samoa.

Over the following centuries these islands became the homeland of the Polynesian peoples. From here their descendants later set out on the voyages that led to the settlement of East Polynesia.
sum: Nukuleka, a village on the lagoon of Tongatapu, is held by many archaeologists to be the first human settlement in Polynesia. People of the Lapita culture lived there from about 2,800 years ago.
